full_judgment: 2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the predecessor of the petitioner and respondent No.6 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.36 of 2000 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Brahmanbaria for partition of the scheduled suit property in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit land of No.10 Beerchandra Mouza within Police Station-Akhaura (previously Kasba), District-Brahmanbaria was under the Taluk of Afzal Bibi and thereafter, 9.46 acres land has been recorded in 20 plots in settlement khatian. 26 decimals land has been recorded under Plot No.11-7 appertaining to CR Khatian No.2. The plaintiffs have been claiming (86¼ +19)=105¼ decimals land out of 9.56 acres land described in the schedule of the plaint. The land in item No.21 has been recorded in Rayati Khatian No.2 in the name of Omed Ali. Bhanu Bibi, Nasimemessa, Sunai Bibi, Zulfigur Ali, Meer Taleb Ali, Meer Akmal Ali, Meer Aynul Uddin Chowdhury were the tenant under Taluk No.10 of Afzal Bibi, Bhanu Bibi and Nasimernessa died issueless and their share has been inherited by Sunai Chand Bibi who died leaving behind two sons, namely, Suruj Mia Chowdhury and Lal Mia Chowdhury as heirs who being owners transferred their shares vide saf-kabala deed No.1230 dated 17.02.1925 to Monohar Ali, father of plaintiff No. 1. Monohar Ali transferred the said land to Ali Newaj vide registered deed No.1227 dated 16.03.1934 and delivered possession. Zulfigur Ali transferred the rest 46¼ decimals land to Monohar Ali, father of plaintiff No.1 vide saf-kabala deed No.2566 dated 06.07.1908 and delivered possession. Ali Newaj and Monohar Ali were in ejmali possession in their purchased property. Omed Ali being owner of 26 decimals land in Plot No. 107/2 died leaving behind only daughter-Sreemoti Ebader Nessa who sold 19 decimals land out of 26 decimals land in favour of Monohar Ali, the grandfather of plaintiff No.1 vide deed No.416 dated 31.01.1934 and delivered possession. In this way, Monohar Ali remained owner and possessor of 105¼ decimals land in Plot No. 214/12 who died leaving behind only daughter, Samider Nessa as heir. Samider Nessa died leaving behind the plaintiffs as heirs. The plaintiffs claimed for partition of the suit land, but the defendants did not agree and hence this suit.
